newsitem.title: INDIA: SBI forex loans to resident Indians.
newsitem.headline: SBI forex loans to resident Indians.

text.p: The State Bank of India (SBI) said on Tuesday it had finalised a scheme for granting loans in foreign currency to resident Indians.

"SBI has finalised its FCNR (B) loans scheme for sanctioning loans in US dollars and pound sterling to resident Indians for working capital purposes and for purchasing capital goods," it said in a statement.
These loans would not require approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) or the Indian government, SBI said.

The RBI had in its monetary policy statement of October 19 allowed banks to lend loans in foreign currency from their deposits under the FCNR (B) scheme (foreign currency non-resident deposits (banks)).
"Preference will be given to exporters and tourism related industries who would be able to effect repayment in foreign currency," the SBI statement said.

Borrowers with no foreign exchange income would have to purchase the foreign currency on the due date of repayment and would have to bear the exchange risk involved. Forward contracts could be booked to cover the exchange risk, the statement added.
It said the loans sanctioned under the scheme would only be by way of demand loans to be carved out of the existing bank limits and term loans would be given for a maximum of three years only.
"The loans will be sanctioned for a minimum amount of US $500,000," SBI said.
Interest on the loans would be linked to LIBOR for the working capital loans and to the corresponding FCNR (B) deposits rates for term loans.
SBI said the loans would be available only at designated branches and would have a prepayment facility for which a penalty would be levied.
